title: Model-based influences on humans' choices and striatal prediction errors
institution: Neuron (Elsevier); author manuscript deposited in PubMed Central
description: Empirical paper. Seventeen adults performed a 201-trial two-stage Markov decision task during fMRI: a first-stage choice leads to one of two second-stage states with fixed 70 percent common transitions, and second-stage options pay money with probabilities that drift as Gaussian random walks between .25 and .75. Model-free reinforcement predicts only a main effect of the previous reward on repeating the first-stage choice; model-based evaluation predicts a reward-by-transition interaction. Choices showed both. A hybrid of model-based learning and SARSA(lambda), weighted by a free parameter w, was fitted per subject by maximum likelihood and compared with nested models; ventral striatal BOLD reflected both model-free and model-based predictions.
